nodes.text: Let $t\geq 1$ and let $d_t$ be the density of the set of integers $n\in\mathbb{N}$ for which $t$ can be represented as the sum of distinct divisors of $n$. Do there exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that\[d_t \sim \frac{c_1}{(\log t)^{c_2}}\]as $t\to \infty$?

#859 : [Er70] number theory | divisors Erdős [Er70] proved that $d_t$ always exists, and that there exist some constants $c_3,c_4>0$ such that\[\frac{1}{(\log t)^{c_3}} < d_t < \frac{1}{(\log t)^{c_4}}.\] Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
